title: Zuri Had a Little Lamb - A Happy Sing-Along Song for Toddlers
description: The little lamb follows along everywhere! Clap your hands and sing this classic with us. #kidssong #nurseryrhyme #toddlersongs #singalong #animalsong
characters: Three adorable Black toddlers: Zuri, a 3-year-old girl with deep warm brown skin, round afro puffs tied with soft yellow fabric scrunchies, wearing a sunny yellow t-shirt, denim dungaree shorts and white sneakers; Kofi, a 4-year-old boy with medium-deep brown skin, short dark natural curly hair, wearing a blue t-shirt, grey jogger shorts and red sneakers; and Nala, a 3-year-old girl with deep brown skin, neat cornrow braids, wearing a yellow pinafore dress over a white t-shirt, white tights and pink sneakers

lines: Its fleece was white as snow
The lamb was sure to go
verses.scene: Zuri walks along a sunny country path with a fluffy white cartoon lamb trotting close behind her.

lines: He followed her to school one day
It made the children laugh and play
To see a lamb at school
verses.scene: The lamb peeks around the doorway of a bright little schoolroom while Kofi and Nala laugh and point.

lines: Little lamb, come sing with me
Clap your hands and count to three
verses.scene: The three toddlers kneel in the grass around the lamb, clapping their hands and counting on their fingers.

lines: And so the teacher turned him out
He waited on the step outside
verses.scene: The lamb waits patiently on the grass outside a low window, tail wagging, while sunshine falls across the yard.

lines: Little lamb, come sing with me
Clap your hands and count to three
verses.scene: The three toddlers kneel in the grass around the lamb, clapping their hands and counting on their fingers.

pd_source.author: Sarah Josepha Hale
pd_source.publication: Poems for Our Children (Boston: Marsh, Capen & Lyon, 1830)
pd_source.public_domain: Published 1830; Hale died 1879. Expired copyright in the US (pre-1929) and worldwide (life+70 ended 1949).
pd_source.adaptation: Hale's stanzas 1-3, with two changes: the name 'Mary' is replaced with 'Zuri' throughout so the song stars this channel's fixed cast rather than introducing an outside character, and stanza 1's 'And everywhere that Mary went' keeps Hale's wording with only that substitution. The two-line hook is NEWLY WRITTEN. Hale's stanzas 4-6 (the teacher's moral) are dropped for length.

song_style: children's nursery rhyme, cheerful upbeat kids song, cute female child voice, simple very repetitive catchy melody, gentle bouncy tempo, playful, bright, warm
